dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Data from EU-funded Aggressotype and MATRICS projects collected across nine sites in Europe (Nijmegen, Mannheim, Barcelona, Madrid, London for functional data; additional sites for anatomical data). Not a publicly named dataset but a consortium-based multi-site collection.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Participants in the current study were part of the EU-funded Aggressotype and MATRICS projects." "In total 208 participants (129 cases, 79 controls) aged 8-18 years were assessed using functional MRI (fMRI) and anatomical scans were acquired in n = 248 (154 cases, 94 controls) across nine sites in Europe."

answer.Aggressotype and MATRICS: normative model training and testing (whole cohort used as reference under 10-fold CV)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The entire cohort (both typically developing controls and DBD cases) was used as a reference for the normative model due to small sample size. Predictions were derived under 10-fold cross-validation. Functional data (n=129) and anatomical data (n=127, intersection with functional) were used for normative modeling and linked ICA integration.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Here, we used the whole cohort (both TD and DBD) as a reference due to the small sample size of the intersection between anatomical and functional data implying that the frequency of DBD in the normative model (n = 77) is higher than in the control population, which means that results ought to be interpreted with respect to this specific cohort. Note that in our analysis GPR predictions are derived in an unbiased manner under 10-fold cross-validation."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Holz2023.pdf.md: Method / Constructing normative models of brain structure and function, L79

model-1.train-phase: NR (10-fold CV used, no separate train/test split reported)

model-2.overall-phase: 127 (whole cohort, 2 excluded for bad image quality from n=129)
model-2.train-phase: NR (10-fold CV used, no separate train/test split reported)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: IMPORTANT: This study used the WHOLE cohort (both healthy controls and DBD cases) as reference, NOT only healthy controls. The n=129 (functional) and n=127 (anatomical) include both 52 controls and 77 cases for the functional model. HC-only N would be 52 for functional model. For the larger anatomical dataset (n=248 before intersection), controls were n=94 and cases n=154. Sensitivity analysis with HC-only reference showed similar results.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "A model of brain development as a function of age and sex was created by training a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model... on a sample of n = 129 and n = 127 (77 cases, Table 1, online Supplementary Fig. S3 for an age distribution) to predict brain function and structure, respectively." "Here, we used the whole cohort (both TD and DBD) as a reference due to the small sample size..."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Holz2023.pdf.md: Method / Constructing normative models of brain structure and function, L79

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Weighted mean calculated from: Controls (n=52): mean=13.88, SD=2.44; Cases (n=77): mean=13.48, SD=2.58. Weighted mean = (52*13.88 + 77*13.48)/129 = 13.64. Pooled SD = sqrt(((52-1)*2.44^2 + (77-1)*2.58^2)/(129-2)) = 2.53. Age range 8-18 years explicitly stated in methods.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "In total 208 participants (129 cases, 79 controls) aged 8-18 years were assessed using functional MRI (fMRI)" "Age, mean (S.D.): Control (n = 52): 13.88 (2.44); Case (n = 77): 13.48 (2.58)"
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.location: Holz2023.pdf.md: Method / Study sample, L61; Table 1, L97-103

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: For functional model (n=129): Males reported - Controls: 34 (65.4%), Cases: 64 (83.1%). Total males = 34+64 = 98. Total females = 129-98 = 31. Female % = 31/129 = 24.0%. For anatomical model (n=127): similar proportions assumed (2 fewer participants due to exclusion for bad image quality). Female count derived by subtraction from total.
